editorial.summary: The 2:35 official trailer for Dirty Hands: The Art and Crimes of David Choe. It begins with production cues and a first-person spray-painting/property-destruction statement with censored and damaged words. A promotional montage then praises David as a standout student with a “dirty” direct style, attributes a 70–80-foot wall to him, emphasizes work ethic, shirt sales/relatability and “bad boy” genius. A first-person Japan account follows: airport hesitation, arrest within 24 hours and three months in jail, then private relationship loss, lifetime reckoning and unlearning. The final prison reflection invokes a Bible, copied verses, identity/belief questions, “every aspect” being illegal and inability to continue. Every idea remains. Multiple voices, praise, dimensions, sales, arrest facts, private girlfriend feelings, conversion and redemption remain attributed/unverified; zero named turns and enrollment windows ship.
